IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE. Branch: worktree-knots-0b4c-lease-owner (commit 8a0e61cbc155, pushed to origin). Worktree: /home/cartine/knots-0b4c-lease-owner.

WHAT LANDED
- src/machine.rs (new): machine_id(store_root) resolves KNOTS_MACHINE_ID -> .knots/machine-id -> salted sha256 of /etc/machine-id (or a random uuid) truncated to 32 hex, persisted on first use. resolve_machine_id takes the env value as a parameter so no test mutates process env.
- src/domain/lease.rs: LeaseOwner{machine_id,pid} + LeaseData.owner (serde default, skip_serializing_if none) + LeaseData::is_owned_by, which returns true when owner is None so legacy events stay local.
- src/lease.rs: create_lease stamps owner{app.machine_id(), process::id()}; new list_local_active_leases(app).
- src/app.rs: App::machine_id().
- src/db/catalog.rs: count_local_active_leases(conn, machine_id) sharing the active-lease predicate plus COALESCE(json_extract(lease_data_json,'$.owner.machine_id'), ?1) = ?1.
- src/replication.rs: require_no_active_leases and sync_or_defer_with_progress both go through a new count_local_active_leases() helper.
- UI: kno show gains a lease_owner field; ui::format_lease_row labels each lease 'this machine' / 'another machine'.
- docs/leases.md: new 'Lease ownership' section. Changeset: .changeset/lease-owner-machine-id.md.

DESIGN DECISIONS FOR THE REVIEWER
1. Only ONE list helper exists (lease::list_local_active_leases). I dropped the db-level list variant the plan sketched because it had no production consumer and would have been dead code under clippy -D warnings. count is the db primitive; list is the App primitive.
2. kno lease list (no flag) now lists leases held by THIS machine, and prints 'no active leases held by this machine' when empty. --all still shows every lease, each labelled with its owner, so foreign leases remain visible. This diverges from my own plan-review directive, which said to keep foreign leases in the default listing; I changed it because the default listing answers 'what is blocking me here'. Please confirm or push back.
3. kno doctor stuck_leases still uses the owner-blind count_active_leases, per the plan-review scope directive. That means doctor can warn about a foreign lease that kno lease list no longer shows. Left deliberately for knots-ec23/knots-0f9c.
4. Replicated leases arrive with lease_expiry_ts = 0 (expiry is local-only DB state, never an event), so the replication test sets a live expiry explicitly to isolate ownership as the reason sync stays unblocked. The test comments say so.

VALIDATION
- make sanity green end to end (fmt, clippy -D warnings, check-changesets, file sizes, 1275+ unit tests + integration + npm test-release, tarpaulin 95.11% vs the 95 gate, +0.01%). The pre-push hook re-ran it on push.
- Manual smoke test on a scratch repo: kno lease create writes .knots/machine-id and stamps the owner; kno lease show prints 'lease_owner: machine=<32 hex> pid=<n>'; rewriting the cached owner to another machine makes kno lease list report none and lets kno sync proceed past the lease guard.
- New tests: src/machine_tests.rs (6), src/domain/lease.rs (5), src/db/tests_lease_owner.rs (4), src/app/tests_list_lease.rs (2), src/replication/tests_lease_owner.rs (2, full event->push->pull->knot_hot round trip), src/ui_tests_ext.rs (4). Verification steps 1-4 all covered.

NOTE ON PROCESS: lease c1ef expired mid-implementation (600s default) and the knot auto-recovered to ready_for_implementation; I re-claimed with a fresh 5400s lease (3a34) rather than reusing the dead one. No work was lost. Later states should use a long timeout.
